title: Josh Hoey Sets 800m World Indoor Record: 1:42.50
excerpt: Josh Hoey ran 1:42.50 in Boston to break Kipketer's 800m world indoor record; Hobbs Kessler set a 2000m world best. What even pacing does for you.
body:
At the New Balance Indoor Grand Prix in Boston on January 24, 2026, Josh Hoey ran 1:42.50 for 800m, breaking Wilson Kipketer's world indoor record of 1:42.67, which had stood since 1997. His brother Jaxson paced him through 400m in 50.02, and Hoey ran the second lap alone.

Earlier at the same meet, Hobbs Kessler ran 4:48.79 for 2000m, beating Kenenisa Bekele's world indoor best of 4:49.99 from 2007, with Grant Fisher second.

Hoey's race shows how much a controlled first lap matters. A well-judged first half leaves you able to hold your speed to the finish instead of slowing down.

In your own hard efforts, focus on the middle of the session or race. Keep your breathing controlled and your form relaxed as the pace starts to hurt. That composure is what lets you finish strongly.

Sources: World Athletics; LetsRun.com
keyTakeaway: Fast times come from a controlled first half, not just a strong finish.
